turns.content: I've been listening to a podcast about astronomy and it's completely rekindled my interest in space.
Astronomy has that effect — the scale of it puts everything in a different perspective. Which podcast?
Planetary Radio. They cover missions, discoveries, a lot of interviews with scientists. Very accessible.
The interview format works well for making technical topics approachable. Any particular topic that's grabbed you?
The James Webb telescope images. I knew they'd be significant but seeing them was genuinely emotional.
There's something about those deep field images — the sheer density of galaxies in what looks like empty sky — that is hard to process.
I went out with binoculars last week to look at the moon. First time I'd done that in maybe twenty years.
The moon through binoculars is always a bit of a revelation. Once you can see craters it stops being a flat circle.
